messages.content: How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?

function.name: thermodynamics_calc_gas_pressure
function.description: Calculate gas pressure in a closed chamber due to heating Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

volume.description: The volume of the chamber in cubic meters. This is a float type value.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

initial_pressure.description: The initial pressure of the gas in Pascal. Default is standard atmospheric pressure. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?" They want to know how much gas is generated. But the chamber is closed, so no gas is generated; the amount of gas remains constant. The question might be about expansion or pressure change. The user might be confused. We can clarify that no gas is generated; the amount stays the same. The pressure will increase. We can compute the new pressure using ideal gas law. The initial pressure is standard atmospheric pressure (101325 Pa). The initial temperature is 25°C (298.15 K). The final temperature is 100°C (373.15 K). The volume is constant. So P_final = P_initial * T_final / T_initial. That yields ~101325 * 373.15 / 298.15 = ~126,700 Pa. So the pressure increases by ~25%. The amount of gas (in moles) remains constant. We can compute the moles: n = P_initial * V / (R * T_initial). R = 8.314 J/(mol*K). So n = 101325 * 2 / (8.314 * 298.15) = ~86.5 mol. So the amount of gas remains 86.5 mol. The user might want to know the mass of gas. The mass of air per mole is ~28.97 g/mol. So mass = 86.5 * 28.97 g = ~2507 g = 2.507 kg. So the mass remains constant. So answer: no gas is generated; the amount remains constant. The pressure increases. Provide the calculation.
